name: Ibb
registryBasis: The national General Authority for Lands, Survey & Urban Planning (GALSUP) is responsible for land and real-estate registration, and Yemeni law recognizes land/register records. The official National Information Center contacts page lists an Ibb coordination office, but that is an information-center office, not evidence of a local land-registry branch. No official city-specific GALSUP Ibb office/service evidence was verified, so local registry presence remains unresolved.
pointBasis: UN WUP 2025 population-weighted settlement centroid; this is not a municipal boundary or a parcel-coverage claim.
technicalBlocker: No anonymous public parcel geometry or safe parcel schema was verified. Local registry basis is unresolved because the only directly verified Ibb office is the National Information Center, not GALSUP.
scopeLimits: Source discovery only. Official evidence confirms local registry/land-record services only where stated in registryBasis; it does not establish complete citywide cadastral coverage or parcel geometry at the WUP point. No owner, address, tax, personal-identity, credential or account lookup was submitted or retained. No parcel geometry or feature attributes were retained.

officialSources.observation: The official GALSUP site is the national authority portal and publishes land-authority notices; no Ibb-specific registry or map service was identified in the reviewed material.
The official Ministry of Justice land/real-estate law is national legal background, not proof of an Ibb city registry or open geometry.
The official Yemen National Information Center lists an Ibb coordination-office address at the governorate building in Al Dhihar; this is the center’s own local office, not a land registry.
